chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his fathers (peace be upon them) that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:
Regarding a man who converted to Islam in the middle of the month of Ramadan, indeed he is not obligated except for what he faces (i.e., the remainder of the month).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting for someone who converts to Islam in the middle of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the obligation of fasting applies prospectively from the moment of conversion, absolving the new Muslim of making up the missed days of Ramadan. This ruling highlights the principle of gradual obligation in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring that the burden of worship is not imposed retroactively on those who were previously exempt due to disbelief. It underscores the mercy inherent in the legal framework, where the transition from non-Muslim to Muslim does not carry a penalty for the period of prior ignorance.
